turns.text: The previous story examined Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks. Now the camera turns to R-CNN and a new question along the same timeline: If we take R-CNN apart, which idea truly changed the direction of research?

Object detection lagged behind image classification because a detector had to localize many possible objects as well as recognize them. R-CNN connected region proposals with features transferred from a large pretrained convolutional network.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?

The system generates candidate regions, warps each region to a fixed size, extracts CNN features, and classifies the regions with category-specific models. Bounding-box regression then refines the proposed locations.

Experts generally treat R-CNN as the starting point of the modern region-based detector family. Its accuracy gains were decisive even though repeated CNN computation made the original pipeline slow and cumbersome.
Seen alongside Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks, R-CNN reveals how the same technical question can echo across different eras.
